body.box_text: For the latest data about the cost of living read our bulletins on;

body.h4: Overview
Overview
body.text: The cost of living has risen in the UK and across the world since 2022.

body.h4: Overview
body.text: Food and energy prices rose markedly, particularly gas prices, partly in response to the conflict in Ukraine. Global recovery from the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic put further pressure on prices.

body.h4: Overview
body.text: In the UK, prices of consumer goods and services rose by 9.6% in the year to October 2022 – the fastest rate in four decades. Since then the annual inflation rate, as measured by the Consumer Prices Index including owner occupier’s housing costs (CPIH), has slowed.

body.h4: Overview
body.text: In the year to January 2024 the annual CPIH inflation rate was 4.2%, unchanged from the previous two months.

body.h4: Overview
body.text: You can explore how the prices of over 450 items in the inflation basket have increased over the past year with our [shopping prices comparison tool](https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/inflationandpriceindices/articles/shoppingpricescomparisontool/2023-05-03).

body.h4: Overview
body.text: You can use our [Personal Inflation Calculator](https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/inflationandpriceindices/articles/howisinflationaffectingyourhouseholdcosts/2022-03-23) to get your own, personalised inflation rate based on what you spend your money on.

body.h4: Overview
Housing: House prices fall while private rents continue to see record rise
body.text: Housing: House prices fall while private rents continue to see record rise

body.h4: Housing: House prices fall while private rents continue to see record rise
body.text: [Average UK house prices](https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/inflationandpriceindices/bulletins/housepriceindex/latest) are estimated to have fallen 1.4% in the year to December 2023 (provisional estimate). This is up from a decrease of 2.3% in the 12 months to November 2023 (revised estimate).

body.h4: Housing: House prices fall while private rents continue to see record rise
body.text: Private rental prices continued to grow at a record high rate in the UK, rising by [6.2% (provisional estimate) in the year to January 2024](https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/inflationandpriceindices/bulletins/indexofprivatehousingrentalprices/latest), unchanged for the second consecutive month. This remains the highest annual percentage change since this UK data series began in January 2016.

Food: Inflation falls to lowest level since April 2022
body.text: Food: Inflation falls to lowest level since April 2022

body.h4: Food: Inflation falls to lowest level since April 2022
body.text: Prices of food and non-alcoholic beverages rose by 7.0% in the year to January 2024 according to the latest [Consumer Prices Index including owner occupiers’ housing costs (CPIH)](https://www.ons.gov.uk/releases/consumerpriceinflationukjanuary2024).

body.h4: Food: Inflation falls to lowest level since April 2022
body.text: This was the tenth consecutive month of falls in food and non-alcoholic beverage inflation, down from 8.0% in December and a recent high of 19.2% in March 2023, which was the highest annual rate seen for over 45 years.

Energy: Around 4 in 10 energy bill payers struggling to afford payments
body.text: Energy: Around 4 in 10 energy bill payers struggling to afford payments

body.h4: Energy: Around 4 in 10 energy bill payers struggling to afford payments
body.text: Around 4 in 10 adults (41%) who pay energy bills said it was very or somewhat difficult to afford them.

body.h4: Energy: Around 4 in 10 energy bill payers struggling to afford payments
body.text: This was according to those asked between 17 and 28 January 2024 as part of our latest [Public opinions and social trends bulletin](https://www.ons.gov.uk/releases/publicopinionsandsocialtrendsgreatbritain17to28january2024).

body.h4: Energy: Around 4 in 10 energy bill payers struggling to afford payments
body.text: This proportion was at a high of 49% in the period covering 17 to 29 May 2023, but appears to have slowly decreased since then.

body.h4: Energy: Around 4 in 10 energy bill payers struggling to afford payments
body.text: The survey also revealed that 44% of adults in Great Britain are using less fuel, such as gas or electricity, in their homes because of the rising cost of living.
